evidence_status: Documentation reviewed; create-expo-app 5.1.5 `default@sdk-58` scaffold generated. npm install succeeded; Expo Doctor passed 20/20; `expo export --platform ios` produced a JS bundle. Generated `npm run lint` and direct TypeScript/lint checks exposed template errors; no native build or device/store qualification.

starting_points.name: Official create-expo-app default template
starting_points.when: A new Expo/React Native application targeting iOS and Android; use a new, absent project directory and review the current default template before accepting it.
steps: Install a supported Node.js LTS and inspect the current create-expo-app help. During the SDK 58 transition, pin `--template default@sdk-58` when SDK 58 is intended: the current Expo docs say unqualified `@latest` creates SDK 57. Record the resolved CLI and generated Expo SDK/React Native versions; `@latest` is still a scaffold-time lookup, not a project dependency pin.

Run the initializer from a source-workspace parent into a destination that does not exist. The current CLI has --no-agents-md but no --no-git flag; the reviewed default created its own .git repository and initial commit. Decide repository ownership before placing it inside another checkout.

Pass --no-agents-md to avoid generating AGENTS.md and Claude settings. Inspect the generated README, app configuration, package scripts, route structure, app identifiers and Git state before adding product code.
Review whether the default universal template's web target is wanted. This profile covers the iOS and Android clients; a web surface needs its own rendering, hosting and browser requirements.

Install dependencies from the generated project root and keep the generated lockfile. Use the generator's SDK-compatible versions as the starting baseline; do not independently upgrade React Native or native modules without checking the Expo SDK matrix.

commands.cwd: A local source-workspace parent; no application files are changed
commands.purpose: Inspect installed-version template choices and flags before creating a project. The 23 October 2026 CLI 5.1.5 help includes --no-agents-md and no --no-git option.

commands.cwd: A local source-workspace parent; mobile-app must not already exist
commands.purpose: Generate the SDK 58 default Expo project while suppressing generated AGENTS.md and Claude settings. During the documented SDK 58 transition, explicitly pin `default@sdk-58`; inspect generated files and repository state. Defer dependency installation so the next step installs packages once from the generated project root.
Install the generated package manifest and create the project's lockfile. Keep the resolved versions in that lockfile.
Check that installed Expo/React Native packages match the selected SDK; inspect installed-version help if the command differs.

notes: Observed 23 October 2026 with the explicit `default@sdk-58` template: create-expo-app 5.1.5 generated Expo SDK 58.0.17, React Native 0.88.0, React 19.3.0 and Expo Router 58.0.25 in package.json. npm install completed; Expo Doctor passed 20/20; `npx expo export --platform ios` emitted a JS bundle. Generated `npm run lint` failed with a version-check error despite ESLint 9.39.5 being installed; direct ESLint found a generated React Hooks rule violation, and `tsc --noEmit` found generated CSS/type compatibility errors. These checks do not establish native build/device compatibility.

The reviewed `default@sdk-58` command with --no-install and --no-agents-md created .git/ with an initial commit. Current help exposed no --no-git option. For a monorepo, decide the intended Git root before generation and resolve nested Git ownership explicitly; never run the initializer over an existing application.

Expo docs state that during the SDK 58 transition `create-expo-app@latest` without `--template` creates SDK 57; pin `--template default@sdk-58` when SDK 58 is the intended baseline. The pinned template was successfully generated in a disposable directory on 23 October 2026.
The default template includes Expo Router, TypeScript and a web target. The existence of generated web files does not qualify a browser product or make this profile a web-stack recommendation.

Expo Go is a limited playground with a fixed set of native libraries. Production development should use a development build; custom native code and native dependencies absent from Expo Go require one.

Default CNG projects generate native iOS/Android directories from app config and plugins. Prefer config plugins for repeatable project configuration; direct edits to generated native directories can be overwritten by prebuild.
`--no-install` can defer npm and native package installation when inspecting a disposable scaffold; install and verify the actual project's dependencies before developing.

follow_up_generators.name: Expo development build and native projects
follow_up_generators.when: The app needs a native module not bundled in Expo Go, custom native code, native configuration, app identity changes to verify, or representative production-like testing.
steps: Check the selected library's iOS and Android support, config plugin, Expo SDK compatibility, minimum OS/SDK and required permissions.

Choose a local native toolchain or an explicitly selected EAS cloud build. Local iOS building requires macOS/Xcode; local Android building requires Android Studio, Android SDK and a compatible Java toolchain. Cloud builds move compilation to EAS but do not eliminate device tests, app-account ownership or store credentials.
Generate native directories/build a development client using the project's current Expo CLI and documented workflow. Review generated diffs; use config plugins for repeatable native configuration.
Install and exercise the development build on both platforms. Rebuild after changes to native dependencies, plugins or app configuration.

commands.purpose: Generate native iOS and Android projects from the Expo app configuration when the project needs native project inspection or customization. Review the diff and use config plugins for repeatable changes.

commands.cwd: The generated mobile-app directory on macOS with compatible Xcode and iOS platform support installed
commands.purpose: Build and launch the iOS app locally for a simulator or configured device. This is not an App Store-signed release.

commands.cwd: The generated mobile-app directory with a compatible Android SDK/JDK and emulator or device configured
commands.purpose: Build and launch the Android app locally. Discover the actual variant/toolchain and inspect the generated Gradle project.
Diagnose app config, dependency compatibility and common project health issues; it does not replace native builds or device checks.

notes: Expo Go cannot load arbitrary native code. Rebuild the development client when the native dependency set or native configuration changes.

When using Continuous Native Generation, generated android/ios directories are normally regenerated from app config and plugins. Keep intentional platform customization reproducible and review source-control ownership before committing generated native projects.

EAS Build is optional. Account linking, build credentials, signing, push credentials and store submission are separate project decisions; this guidance does not create accounts or establish release readiness.

follow_up_generators.name: App-local Expo native module
follow_up_generators.when: A requirement genuinely needs custom Swift or Kotlin native functionality and no maintained compatible module meets it; use a local module when only this application needs it.

commands.purpose: Use Expo's documented local-module generator to create an app-local native module; inspect current CLI help and generated iOS/Android code before adopting it.

notes: A local module introduces native code and needs development builds plus testing on each supported platform. It is not needed for ordinary JavaScript/TypeScript application logic.

The Expo Modules API creates Swift and Kotlin module code. Follow current official documentation and generated examples; do not hand-invent project integration or assume one platform implementation covers the other.

preserve: Keep the generated package manifest, lockfile, Expo app configuration, route structure, TypeScript configuration, assets, scripts and SDK-compatible dependency set; record intentional changes.

Preserve the selected Git repository boundary. The current create-expo-app CLI has no documented --no-git option and the reviewed scaffold created an initial Git repository and commit; inspect this before adding it to a monorepo or existing source tree.
Keep platform identifiers, entitlements, permission descriptions, config plugins, native modules and app-version/build-number policy explicit and compatible with both targets.

Do not commit signing keys, local credentials, generated caches or machine-specific SDK paths. Preserve the project lockfile, build configuration and any native project sources the team has chosen to maintain.
verification: Record create-expo-app version, selected template, resolved Expo SDK/React Native/React versions, package manager and installed runtime; inspect the actual generated baseline before editing.
Run the selected Expo compatibility check and Expo Doctor; retain output and resolve version/configuration warnings before native work.

Build/install a development build for iOS and Android. Exercise the same core journeys with both platform navigation, permissions, lifecycle, offline/reconnect and accessibility behavior; a JavaScript bundle or Expo Go pass does not qualify these native targets.
Test the oldest supported iOS/Android versions and current representative devices. Verify app links, push/permission flows and native SDK integrations only when included in the product scope.

Before a release, verify bundle/application identifiers, signing ownership, version/build numbers, privacy declarations, store listing ownership and install/update behavior on both platforms. A local build or cloud build is not store publication.

sources.title: Expo: create-expo-app and SDK 58 template selection
Expo: Develop an app with Expo

integration_steps: From the generated project root, record app identifiers, supported platforms/OS versions, runtime, Expo SDK, API contract, permissions and build owner in the project's README. Keep the actual generated lockfile.

Select the backend independently. Keep database writes, user/resource authorization, AI/provider secrets, email and durable work server-side. Define versioned API responses and controlled client error handling; a mobile app binary is inspectable.

Implement route/screen state and API access behind testable modules. Keep device UI and domain rules separated enough to test shared logic, but do not abstract away meaningful iOS/Android interaction differences.

Add a native dependency only for a stated capability. Check both-platform support, config plugin, SDK compatibility and minimum OS/API before adding it. Build a development client instead of expecting Expo Go to contain it.

If offline behavior is required, specify local sources, accepted stale data, queued operations, conflict resolution, account switching and data deletion before choosing storage libraries. Server remains the authority for protected/shared data.

Run shared unit/API tests and build/install both native targets. Test navigation/back, permission denial, app restart, expired/revoked sessions, network loss/recovery and accessibility with representative emulators/simulators and physical devices.

Separate development, preview and production application identifiers as needed. Establish account/credential ownership, app store policy and update compatibility before preparing signed builds. No integration, signing or release is implied by generation.
